Title: --torch-backend=auto on Windows with CUDA 12.x driver resolves torchvision 0.2.0 (2018)
Text:
--torch-backend=auto on Windows with CUDA 12.x driver resolves torchvision 0.2.0 (2018)

### Summary


I hit this on my RTX 3060 Ti. On Windows with a CUDA 12.x driver (`>=528.33, <580`), `--torch-backend=auto` selects `cu129` first and resolves `torch 2.9.0+cu129` with `torchvision 0.2.0` (from 2018) without any warning.

Linux with CUDA 12.x and Windows with a CUDA 13 driver (`>=580`) are unaffected.

### Platform

Windows x86_64 (CUDA 12.x driver). Observed on a Windows machine with an RTX 3060 Ti; reproduced on macOS 27 arm64 via `--python-platform x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` and `UV_CUDA_DRIVER_VERSION`.

### Version

```
uv 0.13.6 (329bf9448 2026-10-26 aarch64-apple-darwin)
uv 0.12.16 (Homebrew 2026-09-17 aarch64-apple-darwin)
```

### Reproduce

On Windows:

```bash
UV_CUDA_DRIVER_VERSION=560.94 uv pip install torch torchvision --torch-backend=auto
```

On any OS (`requirements.in` contains `torch` and `torchvision`):

```bash
UV_CUDA_DRIVER_VERSION=560.94 uv pip compile requirements.in --torch-backend=auto --python-platform x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
```

- Plain command with no version pins.
- Reproduced with uv 0.13.6 (Python 3.10–3.13) and 0.12.16.
- Reproduced above by simulating the driver via `UV_CUDA_DRIVER_VERSION`, and also observed on a real Windows GPU machine (RTX 3060 Ti).

| Platform & Driver | First-priority Index | Resolved torch | Resolved torchvision |
|---|---|---|---|
| Windows, CUDA 12.x (`>=528.33, <580`) | `cu129` | `2.9.0+cu129` | `0.2.0` |
| Windows, CUDA 13 (`>=580`) | `cu132` | `2.14.1+cu132` | `0.29.1+cu132` |
| Linux, CUDA 12.x | `cu129` | `2.13.0+cu129` | `0.28.0+cu129` |

### Impact

- `uv pip install` and `import torchvision` succeed, and basic transforms still work.
- Fails later at runtime with `ImportError` on modern symbols (`InterpolationMode`, `efficientnet_b0`) and missing `torchvision.ops`.

  ```
  ImportError: cannot import name 'InterpolationMode' from 'torchvision.transforms'
  ImportError: cannot import name 'efficientnet_b0' from 'torchvision.models'
  ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'torchvision.ops'
  ```
- `torch` itself is also outdated: Windows `cu129` stops at 2.9.0, whereas `cu128` has 2.11.0 and `cu126` has 2.14.1.

### Cause

- `WINDOWS_CUDA_VERSIONS` in `crates/uv-torch/src/backend.rs` tries `cu129` before `cu128` and `cu126` (added in #15416).
- On Windows, the `cu129` index stopped receiving updates at torch 2.9.0 and torchvision 0.23.0 (no 0.24.0 build for torch 2.9.0). On Linux, `cu129` still has matching pairs.
- Per PyTorch's [RELEASE.md](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/RELEASE.md), CUDA 12.9 was experimental for 2.8 and is not listed for 2.9 or later.
- All PyTorch indexes still host pure-Python torchvision 0.1.6 (no dependencies) and 0.2.0 (unbounded `torch` requirement) wheels.
- uv fetches torch-family packages from every index in the auto list in order (`cu129` first), and the default index strategy prefers earlier indexes, so 0.2.0 is the first torchvision candidate on `cu129` compatible with torch 2.9.0 (pip on the same index picks 0.1.6). With `--index-strategy unsafe-best-match`, versions across indexes are compared directly, which is why that workaround works.

| Windows Index | Latest torch | Latest torchvision | Resolved Pair (torch + torchvision) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cu126` | `2.14.1+cu126` | `0.29.1+cu126` | `2.14.1+cu126` + `0.29.1+cu126` |
| `cu128` | `2.11.0+cu128` | `0.26.0+cu128` | `2.11.0+cu128` + `0.26.0+cu128` |
| `cu129` | `2.9.0+cu129` | `0.23.0+cu129` (for torch 2.8) | `2.9.0+cu129` + `0.2.0` |

### Workarounds

- `--torch-backend=cu128` → torch `2.11.0+cu128` + torchvision `0.26.0+cu128`
- `--index-strategy unsafe-best-match` → torch `2.14.1+cu126` + torchvision `0.29.1+cu126`
- `torchvision>=0.3` → torch `2.8.0+cu129` + torchvision `0.23.0+cu129`

Related: #12357, #14742, #16386

### Possible fixes

- Lower the priority of (or drop) `cu129` in `WINDOWS_CUDA_VERSIONS`.
- Prefer the next index in the auto list when the first-priority index has no torchvision release paired with the resolved torch version.
- Enforce a minimum version bound for torch-family packages so legacy unpinned wheels (0.1.6 / 0.2.0) are not selected for modern torch.

I would be happy to open a PR for whichever fix you prefer.

Title: Windows trampoline can close its own child or job handle when started through the C runtime's spawn, so the child is lost
Text:
Windows trampoline can close its own child or job handle when started through the C runtime's spawn, so the child is lost

### Summary

When a venv's `python.exe` (the uv trampoline) is started through the C runtime's spawn functions, such as Python's `os.spawnv(os.P_WAIT, ...)`, it sometimes returns before the Python it launched has run. It does so in one of two ways:

- exit code 1, with `uv trampoline failed to get exit code of child process` / `Caused by: uncategorized error (os error 6)`;
- exit code 0, with the child terminated before it ran.

CPython's own venv launcher and the base interpreter never do this under the same conditions.

### Reproduction

```python
# repro.py: python repro.py <path to a python.exe> [pipes] [spawns]
import collections, msvcrt, os, sys, tempfile, _winapi

python = sys.argv[1]
pipes = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 500
spawns = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 200
# What subprocess does with a pipe: a handle that is not inheritable, wrapped as a
# C-runtime descriptor with msvcrt.open_osfhandle(handle, 0).
fds = [msvcrt.open_osfhandle(h, 0) for _ in range(pipes) for h in _winapi.CreatePipe(None, 0)]
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
lost = collections.Counter()
for i in range(spawns):
    out = os.path.join(d, f"{i}.txt")
    # os.spawn* joins its arguments unquoted: no spaces in the code.
    rc = os.spawnv(os.P_WAIT, python, [python, "-c", f"open(r'{out}','w').close()"])
    if not os.path.exists(out):
        lost[rc] += 1
print(f"{sum(lost.values())} of {spawns} spawns returned before the child had run, by exit code: {dict(lost)}")
```

```
uv venv uvvenv
python -m venv stdvenv
python repro.py uvvenv\Scripts\python.exe
python repro.py stdvenv\Scripts\python.exe
```

Whether a run loses children depends on where handle values happen to fall in that process, so run it several times. Five runs of 200 spawns each:

| `python.exe` | Children lost per run |
|---|---|
| uv trampoline | 0, 2, 8, 0, 15 (exit code 0 in 17, exit code 1 in 8) |
| CPython's venv launcher (`python -m venv`) | 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 |
| the base interpreter | 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 |

The trampoline also prints a `Failed to close child file descriptors at N` warning for nearly every descriptor, on every spawn. The other two print nothing and close nothing.

We first saw it as a flaky test on GitHub Actions (`windows-11-arm`, Python 3.11, uv 0.13.5). There a pytest-xdist worker ran `os.spawnv(os.P_WAIT, sys.executable, ...)`, and `sys.executable` was the venv's trampoline:

```
warning: Failed to close child file descriptors at 4
warning: Failed to close child file descriptors at 6
warning: Failed to close child file descriptors at 7
warning: Failed to close child file descriptors at 9
warning: Failed to close child file descriptors at 11
warning: Failed to close child file descriptors at 13
error: uv trampoline failed to get exit code of child process
  Caused by: uncategorized error (os error 6)
```

### Cause

`bounce()` in `crates/uv-trampoline/src/bounce.rs` calls `spawn_child`, creates the job, assigns the child to it, and then calls `close_handles(&si)`. `close_handles` calls `CloseHandle` on every value in the C runtime's `lpReserved2` table from index 3.

Those values are the parent's handles. The trampoline holds only the ones that were inheritable. The parent's C runtime also lists descriptors whose handles are not inheritable: Python's `subprocess` wraps its non-inheritable pipe handles with `msvcrt.open_osfhandle(handle, 0)`, which leaves the C runtime's no-inherit flag clear. Such a value means nothing in the trampoline, which is what the warnings report.

When such a value equals a handle the trampoline has created by then, `CloseHandle` succeeds and closes it:

- **The child's process handle:** `WaitForSingleObject` returns at once, and `GetExitCodeProcess` fails with os error 6.
- **The job handle:** the job has `JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`, so the child is terminated, and the trampoline exits with the child's exit code, 0.

distlib's launcher does the same in the same order (`post_spawn_cleanup` after `CreateProcessW` and `AssignProcessToJobObject` in `PC/launcher.c`), deliberately after spawning (pypa/pip#10444). We have not tested it.

### A possible fix

Before creating any handle of its own, record which values in `lpReserved2` are handles in the trampoline (for example, those for which `GetHandleInformation` succeeds): those are the ones it inherited. After spawning, close only those. A value that was not a handle at startup can then never match the child's or the job's handle. The cleanup still runs after the child has inherited what it needs, as distlib intends.

### Platform

Windows 11 x86_64 (10.0.26300); also GitHub Actions `windows-11-arm`.

### Version

uv 0.13.6 (329bf9448 2026-10-26); also uv 0.13.5. `crates/uv-trampoline/src/bounce.rs` is the same on `main` as in 0.13.5.

### Python version

CPython 3.14.9 (uv-managed); also 3.11.17 on the ARM runner.

### Platform

Windows 11 x86_64 (10.0.26300); also GitHub Actions windows-11-arm

### Version

uv 0.13.6 (329bf9448 2026-10-26); also uv 0.13.5

### Python version

CPython 3.14.9 (uv-managed); also 3.11.17 on the ARM runner
Reply:
`lpReserved2` is coming from the parent process, which can be python, or something else, so while it's reasonable to assume that if it's a pointer it points into a buffer of a given size, it's not reasonable to assume that it will be in the format that MSVC chooses to use, because you can literally smuggle anything there. Or, more likely, as in this case, it contains stale data which isn't valid anymore, and in some cases can overlap with handles that we didn't inherit and that we're using (i.e. the job handle)

The original pr (#1092) added this speculatively based on code that itself didn't seem to know if it needed it, we already close things that it makes sense to close, and we can't truthfully rely on `lpReserved2` to close more things.

I think we can drop that `lpReserved2` code for now...

Title: Add a flag / env var to ignore required-version
Text:
Add a flag / env var to ignore required-version

### Summary

When a project pins uv exactly with `required-version` (for example `required-version = "==0.13.5"`, often so that CI and `astral-sh/setup-uv` with `version-file` use the same uv version), every local command fails as soon as the developer's uv is a patch release ahead:

```
error: Required uv version `==0.13.5` does not match the running version `0.13.6`
```

This happens often when uv comes from a package manager that upgrades it independently and can't run `uv self update`, such as Homebrew. Even `uv help` fails. There is currently no way to run uv:

- `--no-config` gets past the check, but it also drops the rest of `[tool.uv]` (`package`, `default-groups`, `constraint-dependencies`, indexes, ...). That can silently change what gets synced into the environment.
- `uvx uv@<pinned> ...` works, but it has to be wrapped in a shell function that parses `pyproject.toml` for the pin.

I'd like an explicit opt-out for the version check only, with the rest of the configuration still applied. For example:

- a global flag `--no-required-version` (or `--ignore-required-version`)
- an environment variable `UV_NO_REQUIRED_VERSION=1`

uv could still print a warning that the running version doesn't match the requirement, so the user knows they are outside the pin.

### Example

```console
$ uv --version
uv 0.13.6
$ grep required-version pyproject.toml
required-version = "==0.13.5"

$ uv run ruff check .
error: Required uv version `==0.13.5` does not match the running version `0.13.6`

$ uv --no-required-version run ruff check .
warning: Ignoring `required-version` (`==0.13.5`); running uv 0.13.6
All checks passed!

$ UV_NO_REQUIRED_VERSION=1 uv sync --frozen
warning: Ignoring `required-version` (`==0.13.5`); running uv 0.13.6
...
```

Title: Concurrent Git fetches for packages from the same repository race on a cold cache: "failed to remove directory …/git-v1/db/<id>: Directory not empty"
Text:
Concurrent Git fetches for packages from the same repository race on a cold cache: "failed to remove directory …/git-v1/db/<id>: Directory not empty"

### Summary

### Summary

When a project depends on several packages that come from **subdirectories of the same Git repository**, `uv sync --frozen` with a **cold cache** intermittently fails:

```text
error: Failed to download and build `pkg-a @ git+https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git@<sha>#subdirectory=pkg-a`
  cause: Git operation failed
  cause: failed to remove directory `<cache>/git-v1/db/<id>`: Directory not empty (os error 39)
```

A Git trace shows one `git init` creating the repository database while a second Git process inspects the same directory and finds it isn't a repository yet. uv then deletes the directory while the first process is still writing into it. A second run, with the database now present, succeeds.

### Environment

- uv 0.12.24
- Git 2.56.0
- GitHub-hosted runner, `ubuntu-26.04` (image 20261025)
- `UV_CACHE_DIR` inside the workspace, not restored from a previous run (cold)
- Git auto-maintenance disabled in the environment (`maintenance.auto=false`, `gc.auto=0`), so this is not #22829

I haven't reproduced it on 0.13.x. I didn't find a related fix in the 0.13.0–0.13.6 release notes.

### Reproduction shape

A project whose lockfile has three dependencies from one repository, pinned to the same commit:

```toml
[project]
dependencies = ["pkg-a", "pkg-b", "pkg-c"]

[tool.uv.sources]
pkg-a = { git = "https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git", tag = "<tag>", subdirectory = "pkg-a" }
pkg-b = { git = "https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git", tag = "<tag>", subdirectory = "pkg-b" }
pkg-c = { git = "https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git", tag = "<tag>", subdirectory = "pkg-c" }
```

Run `uv sync --frozen` from an empty cache, repeatedly.

Results from 20 parallel CI jobs on the same commit:

| Cache | Failed |
| --- | --- |
| Cold (empty `UV_CACHE_DIR`) | 2 of 10 |
| Restored (database for the repository already present) | 0 of 10 |

### Evidence

With `RUST_LOG=uv_git=debug`, uv logs three fetches for the repository, then a single update:

```text
DEBUG Fetching source distribution from Git: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git
DEBUG Fetching source distribution from Git: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git
DEBUG Fetching source distribution from Git: https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git
DEBUG Updating Git source `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git`
```

`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` shows the overlap. Both failing jobs had the same sequence; times are relative to the `git init`:

| Time | Process | Event |
| --- | --- | --- |
| +0 ms | A | `git init`, `def_repo` = `<cache>/git-v1/db/<id>` |
| +14 ms | B | `git rev-parse` starts |
| +14 ms | B | `error`, exits 128: not a repository yet |
| +240 ms | A | killed (signal), after uv aborted |

So a second task inspected the database while the first was still initializing it, treated it as invalid, and removed it.

### What I looked at

In 0.12.24, `GitResolver::fetch` (`crates/uv-git/src/resolver.rs`) takes an exclusive `LockedFile` on `git-v1/locks/<digest of repository URL>` around `GitSource::fetch`. That lock is keyed the same way as the database path, and `LockedFile` uses `flock`, which should exclude a second task in the same process. The trace nonetheless shows a `git rev-parse` against the database running concurrently with `git init`. I didn't find which code path issues that check, so it may run outside this lock, or the lock may not be held across initialization.

### Workaround

Retrying `uv sync` succeeds once the database exists. A warm cache (restored from a previous run) avoids the failure.


### Platform

ubuntu 26.04 amd64

### Version

0.12.24

### Python version

3.14.9

Title: Modifying a file in a `.venv` silently corrupts the shared cache and all other venvs (hardlink mode), and uv has no way to detect or repair it
Text:
Modifying a file in a `.venv` silently corrupts the shared cache and all other venvs (hardlink mode), and uv has no way to detect or repair it

### Summary

As `uv` uses hardlinks to install files in .venv modifying a file will modify it for all .venv using that package now and in the future.

This happens i.e. when manually doing fast test what upstream changes would do or even unindented if your IDE is not configured correctly and you perform a refactoring.

I didn't find anything besides cleaning the cache and reinstalling all polluted .venv that would fix / reinstall the modified file.

I am used to a similar behaviour in conda but it at least raised SafetyWarnings when this happened. `uv` just stays silent.

### Example

It would be great if uv could use the `.dist-info/RECORD` files to verify that the cache was unmodified. And if not print a warning, removes the package from cache and reinstall it.

> *The following ideas were suggested by Claude (AI). I only include them as options, ordered by preference.*
>
> 1. **`uv sync` (and `uv pip install/sync`) verifies installed packages against their `.dist-info/RECORD`.**
>    A cheap pre-check (size, mtime) could come first, the hash comparison second, or the full check could be opt-in (e.g. `uv sync --verify`).
>    On a mismatch: print a warning, remove the affected package from the cache, and reinstall it.
>    The cache entry must be invalidated too, because in hardlink mode it shares the modified file.
> 2. **A dedicated check command**, e.g. `uv cache check` / `uv cache verify` (cache entries against their `RECORD`) and/or a venv-side option such as `uv sync --check --verify`.
>    It should exit non-zero on a mismatch, with an optional `--fix`.
> 3. **Documentation only:** state in "Cache safety" and in the `link-mode` docs that, with hardlinks, editing a file in a venv also modifies the cache and all other venvs, and describe the recovery steps (`uv cache clean <pkg>`, then `uv sync --reinstall-package <pkg>` in each affected venv).

Title: Scrub home directory path from `uv` output
Text:
Scrub home directory path from `uv` output

### Summary

When I was making https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/22985, I noticed that the output of `uv audit --verbose` included paths prefixed by my full `${HOME}` directory (which I replaced with `~`). I think `uv` should do this itself, since we encourage people to post verbose output in bug reports. This should reduce the amount of personal information that might accidentally get posted online through verbose `uv` output.

### Example

This should be default behavior. Perhaps with a flag to disable it, just in case that's desired for some reason?

A user with the username `jdoe` who previously saw:

```text
DEBUG Found user configuration in: /home/jdoe/.config/uv/uv.toml
```

Would instead see:

```text
DEBUG Found user configuration in: ~/.config/uv/uv.toml
```

Ideally this should take atomic distributions into consideration, where the directory `${HOME}` refers to is a symlink to `/var/${HOME}`. This only affects *some* of the output. My system (which is an atomic distro) produces the user config path as in the first example above, but that same `uv` command also included a path like:

```text
DEBUG Found workspace root: /var/home/jdoe/rust-lang/fls
```

Which, ideally, would also become:

```text
DEBUG Found workspace root: ~/rust-lang/fls
```
Reply: I am wary of this being worth it, the verbose logs already can contain a lot of personal information and they're not designed to be sharable in a de-identified way.

Title: `uvx` "Failed to spawn" on CPython dev builds with `+dev` version suffix
Text:
`uvx` "Failed to spawn" on CPython dev builds with `+dev` version suffix

### Summary

Dev builds of Python 3.14 and earlier have a version ending in `+`:

```console
❯ ./python.exe --version
Python 3.14.8+
```

And uvx runs tools fine:

```console
❯ uvx --python ./python.exe pycowsay hello

  -----
< hello >
  -----
   \   ^__^
    \  (oo)\_______
       (__)\       )\/\
           ||----w |
           ||     ||
```

However, dev builds of 3.15 onwards have a vesion ending in `+dev`:

```console
❯ ./python.exe --version
Python 3.16.0a1+dev
```

This was to make them compatible with PEP 508 versions: https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/99968.

But uvx isn't happy:

```console
❯ uvx --python ./python.exe pycowsay hello
error: Failed to spawn: pycowsay
  cause: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

Reproducible with 3.15 and 3.16, and other tools such as tox, and on Ubuntu on GitHub Actions.


### Platform

macOS 15 (Darwin 24.6.0) arm64; also Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 on GitHub Actions

### Version

uv 0.13.6 (329bf9448 2026-10-26 aarch64-apple-darwin); also uv 0.12.23 on Linux

### Python version

Python 3.16.0a1+dev

Title: Annotated-tag object id given as a git rev fails with "Exact Git revision does not match precise commit"
Text:
Annotated-tag object id given as a git rev fails with "Exact Git revision does not match precise commit"

## Summary

When the `@rev` of a git dependency is the 40-hex id of an **annotated tag object** (what `git rev-parse vX` returns for an annotated tag), uv treats it as an exact commit, fetches it, and then fails because the commit it ends up on is the tag's peeled commit. The error names the right commit but not why the two ids differ, so the pin reads as corrupt rather than as "you pinned the tag object".

## Reproduction

Any public repo with an annotated tag works; `psf/requests` here.

```
$ git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/psf/requests.git 'refs/tags/v2.32.3*'
61e2240f283f15780ac2d0e2cfefb0fd6fdab627	refs/tags/v2.32.3
0e322af87745eff34caffe4df68456ebc20d9068	refs/tags/v2.32.3^{}

$ uvx --no-cache --from "git+https://github.com/psf/requests@61e2240f283f15780ac2d0e2cfefb0fd6fdab627" python -c 'import requests; print(requests.__version__)'
   Updating https://github.com/psf/requests (61e2240f283f15780ac2d0e2cfefb0fd6fdab627)
error: Failed to resolve `--with` requirement
  cause: Git operation failed
  cause: Exact Git revision `61e2240f283f15780ac2d0e2cfefb0fd6fdab627` does not match precise commit `0e322af87745eff34caffe4df68456ebc20d9068` for `https://github.com/psf/requests`

$ uvx --no-cache --from "git+https://github.com/psf/requests@0e322af87745eff34caffe4df68456ebc20d9068" python -c 'import requests; print(requests.__version__)'
2.32.3
```

The peeled commit (`v2.32.3^{commit}`) installs; the tag object id does not.

## Ask

One of:

- peel an annotated-tag object to its commit (the fetch already has the tag object, so the target commit is known), or
- make the error say that the given rev is an annotated-tag object and suggest pinning `vX^{commit}` (or the peeled id shown), and
- a line in the git-dependencies docs that a full-sha pin must be a commit id, and that `git rev-parse <tag>` of an annotated tag is not one.

## Platform

uv 0.13.6 (Homebrew build of 2026-10-26, aarch64-apple-darwin), macOS 26 (Darwin 27.0.0).
Reply:
> * peel an annotated-tag object to its commit (the fetch already has the tag object, so the target commit is known), or

Yeah, I think we should do this. It's (unfortunately) somewhat common for people to use the SHA from an annotated tag or similar without realizing that it's still an indirection vs. the underlying commit.
